newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on improved sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Monday due to improved market sentiment with the end of the long Chinese Lunar New Year break, traders said.
The most active November 1997 contract rose seven yuan to 3,359 yuan ($405) per tonne. It opened at an intra-day low of 3,350 yuan, hitting a high of 3,362 yuan.
March fell 42 yuan to 3,080, May rose 50 to 3,100, July 60 to 3,340, September 13 to 3,350 and January fell one yuan to 3,352.
Combined volume fell to 17,700 tonnes from 76,600.
"More fresh buying has emerged due to improved market sentiment, pushing most prices up," one trader said. "Rises on the Dalian Futures Exchange also helped today's gains."
But he said trading was dull and some time would be needed to reverse the bearish mood.
Traders said prices were likely to firm over the coming few days because of expectations of improved long-term fundamentals.
